tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is moving horizontally with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> extra mass is added, the final velocity (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) is:

solution.text:
From the conservation of linear momentum, it can be written that

Mu=M+mv   ...1

where, M is the initial mass, u is the initial velocity, m is the extra mass added and v is the final velocity of the composition.

From equation (1), it follows that

1000×6=1200×v⇒v=5 m s-1
